description: Given a 0-indexed chord progression, identify the key(s), all ii-V-I / ii-V-i (index triples; strict P4-up then P5-down — tritone subs and V-I without a ii do NOT count), and the Roman numeral per chord. gold.keys is a list of acceptable answers, each an array of key names (a modulation needs all keys in one set; alternative spellings are separate sets).

items.ruleContext: Key: C major. Dm7=ii-7, G7=V7, Cmaj7=Imaj7. Detected 2-5-1: Dm7→G7→Cmaj7 (C major).
Key: G major. Am7=ii-7, D7=V7, Gmaj7=Imaj7. Detected 2-5-1: Am7→D7→Gmaj7 (G major).
Key: Bb major. Cm7=ii-7, F7=V7, Bbmaj7=Imaj7. Detected 2-5-1: Cm7→F7→Bbmaj7 (Bb major).
Key: D minor. Em7b5=iiø7, A7=V7(alt), Dm7=i-7. Detected minor 2-5-1: Em7b5→A7→Dm7 (D minor).
Two key centers. C major (bars 1-3): Dm7=ii-7, G7=V7, Cmaj7=Imaj7. Bb major (bars 4-6): Cm7=ii-7, F7=V7, Bbmaj7=Imaj7. Detected 2-5-1 x2.
Key: C major. Dm7=ii-7, G7=V7, Cmaj7=Imaj7, A7=VI7 (secondary dominant V7/ii, turnaround). One 2-5-1: Dm7→G7→Cmaj7.
Relative major/minor. Bb major: Cm7=ii-7, F7=V7, Bbmaj7=Imaj7, Ebmaj7=IVmaj7. G minor: Am7b5=iiø7, D7=V7(alt), Gm7=i-7. Detected 2-5-1 x2.
Key: F major (blues). All dominant chords. F7=I7, Bb7=IV7. No ii-V-I present.
Key: F major. Gm7=ii-7, C7=V7, Fmaj7=Imaj7. Detected 2-5-1: Gm7→C7→Fmaj7 (F major).
Key: C major. Static Imaj7 vamp. No ii-V-I present.
Key: C major. Cmaj7=Imaj7, A7=VI7 (secondary dominant V7/ii), Dm7=ii-7, G7=V7, Cmaj7=Imaj7. One 2-5-1 at indices 2-3-4 (Dm7→G7→Cmaj7). A7 is NOT a ii.
Key: C major with modal interchange. Cmaj7=Imaj7, Fm7=iv-7 (borrowed from C minor), Bb7=bVII7 (backdoor dominant). Fm7→Bb7 resolves deceptively to Cmaj7 — NOT a ii-V-I in C. No ii-V-I.
Primary key G major: Am7=ii-7, D7=V7, Gmaj7=Imaj7 (2-5-1). Bb7 is a Coltrane-style secondary dominant pivoting toward Eb (V7/Eb) — not part of a ii-V-I here.
Modal: D dorian vamp (Dm7 ↔ Em7, i-7 ↔ ii-7). No dominant, no ii-V-I.
Ab major: Fm7=vi-7, Bbm7=ii-7, Eb7=V7, Abmaj7=Imaj7 (2-5-1 at 1-2-3). Then Dbmaj7=IVmaj7 of Ab. G7→Cmaj7 is a V-I into C major (no ii — NOT a ii-V-I). Detected one 2-5-1: Bbm7→Eb7→Abmaj7.
Key: C major. Dm7=ii-7, Db7=bII7 (tritone substitute of G7, subV7/I), Cmaj7=Imaj7. Db7→Cmaj7 is a half-step resolution, NOT the P5 of a standard ii-V-I, so no ii-V-I is counted.
Key: C minor. Dm7b5=iiø7, G7=V7(alt), Cm7=i-7. Detected minor 2-5-1: Dm7b5→G7→Cm7.
Two key centers. G major: Am7=ii-7, D7=V7, Gmaj7=Imaj7. F major: Gm7=ii-7, C7=V7, Fmaj7=Imaj7. Detected 2-5-1 x2.
Key: C major. Dm7→G7→Cmaj7 is the 2-5-1. Fm7=iv-7, Bb7=bVII7 (backdoor) resolving to Cmaj7 — NOT a ii-V-I. One 2-5-1 only.
Modal: A minor/dorian vamp (i-7 ↔ iv-7). No dominant, no ii-V-I.
Coltrane changes — tonal centers in major thirds. Eb7→Abmaj7 and B7→Emaj7 are V-I motions WITHOUT a preceding ii, so they are NOT ii-V-I. No ii-V-I detected.
Key: C major. Dm7=ii-7, G7=V7 but the progression ends on V7 with NO resolving I — an incomplete ii-V (turnaround). No complete ii-V-I.
Key: C major throughout. Two 2-5-1 cells (indices 0-2 and 4-6); Am7=vi-7 is a passing turnaround chord, not part of either.
Key: A minor. Bm7b5=iiø7, E7=V7(alt), Am7=i-7 (minor 2-5-1) twice; Fmaj7=VImaj7 between them. Detected minor 2-5-1 x2.
